parameters.name: fiber_type
parameters.description: The base fiber material of the fabric, which fundamentally determines its properties and behavior

values.definition: Combed long-staple wool fibers spun into fine, sleek yarn. Short fibers discarded. The standard for quality suiting. Smooth, resilient, drapes well. Super numbers indicate fiber fineness (Super 100s = 18.75 microns through Super 250s = 11.25 microns). Higher super ≠ necessarily better performance.
Carded wool using both short and long fibers. Creates a hairy, softer, loftier fabric. Flannel and most tweeds are woolen. Warmer but less sleek than worsted. Matte finish with melange color effect.

From cashmere goat undercoat. Grade A = 14-16 microns. Extremely soft but poor durability for suiting — pills and bags, especially in trousers. Best in blends (5-10% with worsted adds softness without sacrificing performance) or as standalone jacketings/knitwear.

Hair from Angora goat. Distinctive two-tone luster. Naturally crease-resistant and elastic. Primary summer application — alternative to high-twist wools. Especially valued for dinner jackets (crispness + lightness + glamorous sheen). Modern blends: 5-15% in commercial, 40-70% in British mohairs.

From Merino sheep. Highly crimped fibers (up to 100 crimps per inch). The base fiber for most quality worsted suiting at Super 100s and above. Excellent moisture-wicking. Also used in softer Saxony tweeds.

Versatile plant fiber. Used across the formality spectrum from fine dress shirt broadcloth to casual denim. Breathable, comfortable. Less resilient than wool — wrinkles more easily in lighter weaves. Quality measured by staple length and thread count.

From flax fibers. Strongest natural fiber. Fiber length 18-30 inches. Excellent breathability and heat conductivity — cool to touch. Very poor wrinkle resistance (considered part of its charm). Natural luster. The quintessential warm-weather fabric.

Protein fiber from silkworm cocoons. Strongest natural fiber by weight. Takes dye exceptionally well. Wide range from matte (shantung, raw silk) to high sheen (charmeuse). Used primarily for ties, pocket squares, linings, and formal shirt fronts (pique).

parameters.notes: Natural fibers are universally preferred in classic menswear. Blends can combine the best properties of multiple fibers (e.g., wool-silk-linen for summer, wool-cashmere for luxury).

parameters.name: weave_type
parameters.description: The construction method used to interlace yarns, which determines texture, drape, and durability

values.definition: Simple over-under interlacing. Broadcloth, poplin, tropical wool, hopsack (double plain), fresco. Tightest possible interlacing. Good breathability when open. Most versatile weave.

Diagonal pattern where weft passes over two or more warp yarns. Creates characteristic diagonal lines. Serge (2x2 twill), gabardine (steep warp-face twill), cavalry twill (double twill). More drape than plain weave. Slightly more wrinkle-resistant.
Long float yarns on face creating smooth, lustrous surface. Charmeuse, moleskin (cotton satin weave then shorn). Maximum sheen. Less durable than plain or twill due to exposed floats.
Groups of warp and weft threads interlace as units. Oxford cloth (1x2 basket), hopsack (2x2 basket). More textured than plain weave. Less formal. Good breathability.

Twill weave where the diagonal reverses at regular intervals, creating a V or zigzag pattern. Classic for tweeds and sport coats. Adds visual interest while remaining subtle. Named for resemblance to fish skeleton.

Two warp yarns twist around each weft yarn creating an open, stable mesh. Used for grenadine ties. Woven exclusively in Lake Como, Italy on historic wooden looms. Open structure with distinctive honeycomb/brick-like pattern.

Extra set of yarns creates raised surface — loops (terry) or cut (velvet, corduroy). Corduroy has ridged pile (wales). Velvet has uniform pile. Moleskin has shorn pile. Rich texture, often plush and soft.

Complex weave with raised parallel cords creating a waffle or honeycomb texture. Used for polo shirts and formal Marcella evening shirt fronts. Bridges casual (polo) and very formal (white tie) applications.

parameters.name: suiting_fabric
parameters.description: Fabric types specifically used for suits and sport jackets, with their key characteristics

values.definition: The benchmark suit fabric. Weight range: 180-300g/m (6-10oz). Practical minimum ~210g/7oz. Benchmark 3-season weight ~260g/9oz. Smooth, resilient, drapes well. Clean, sleek appearance. Most formal of common suitings.
Carded or worsted wool with brushed, hairy surface. Soft, matte, warm. Charcoal flannel is office-appropriate. Weight: 10-14oz. Melange color effect from Vigoureux printing process.

High-twist wool in open plain weave. Fresco core: 9-10oz. Dry, rough hand. Matte. Excellent breathability and wrinkle resistance from high-twist yarns that snap back. Summer specialist — too sharp for a sport coat alone, best as full suit.
Wool-mohair blend (5-70% mohair). Distinctive two-tone luster. Crease-resistant. Lighter than equivalent wool. Especially valued for dinner jackets and summer business suits. Glamorous sheen.
2x2 twill weave with identical warp and weft. Weight: 200-300g/m2. Classic for navy blazers and DB suits. Military heritage. Good drape and wrinkle resistance.
Tight twill with warp double the density of weft. Visible diagonal ridges on face. Excellent wrinkle resistance and shape retention. Low breathability (very tight weave). Formal trousers and suits.

Double plain weave (2x2 basket) creating small cube appearance. Less formal than smooth worsted. Open construction for breathability. Versatile blazer fabric — less shiny than traditional blazers. Easy to wear as separates.
Creates circular eye patterns through specific color sequencing. Reads as near-solid from distance. Subtle texture up close. Standard worsted weight and hand.
Hand-woven in Outer Hebrides, 100% virgin wool. Legally protected by Harris Tweed Act 1993 (Orb trademark). Rough, thick, coarse. Water-resistant, windproof. Sport coats and country wear only.
County Donegal, Ireland. Distinctive colorful slubs (thick spots) woven into fabric creating a speckled/flecked effect. Slightly softer than Harris. Sport coats and country wear.
From Cheviot sheep (England-Scotland border). Harder finish than other tweeds. More structured. Durable, weather-resistant.

Flax fiber in plain weave. Weight: 8-9oz (European) to 10-13oz (Irish). Excellent breathability. Very poor wrinkle resistance. Irish linen is denser, wrinkles less, drapes better. Natural slubs and luster.
Puckered plain weave cotton. Two different shrinking fibers create wavy texture. Promotes airflow. Blue-white stripes classic. Hides wrinkles inherently. Summer only.

Pile weave with vertical ridges (wales). Soft, plush. Wales range from narrow/dense to wide-spaced. Earth tones classic. English = stiffer/firmer; Italian = more fluid. Country, casual, sporting wear.

Uniform pile without ridges (unlike corduroy). Luxurious, plush nap. Rich luster. Used for evening jackets and smoking jackets. More formal than corduroy. Dark colors (green, burgundy, navy) for evening.

parameters.name: shirting_fabric
parameters.description: Fabric types specifically used for dress and sport shirts

values.definition: Plain weave, tightly woven. Smoothest of all shirt weaves. Very little sheen. Most prone to wrinkling. Thread counts from 50s singles to 140s+ doubles. Most formal — ideal for business, formal events, weddings.

Diagonal weave. Softer than broadcloth. More wrinkle-resistant and easier to iron. Almost always has a bit of shine — high thread counts may be mistaken for silk. Formal dress shirts appropriate with suits.
Same weave as oxford but finer yarn, tighter weave, higher thread count. Slightly heavier than broadcloth, lighter than oxford. Matte, crisp. Great everyday work shirts — middle formality.

Symmetrical basketweave (1x2). Much heavier/thicker than average shirt fabric. Slightly rough with visible white dot effect. Can be worn slightly wrinkled. Originally developed for sportswear. American button-down staple. Casual/sporty.
Plain weave with colored warp and white weft. Heavier than broadcloth. Soft, casual, varied texture. Sometimes slubby yarns for additional character. Casual/workwear heritage.
Flax fiber plain weave. Excellent breathability and cool hand. Wrinkles heavily but considered characterful. Natural slubs. Summer specialist. Casual.
Twill weave, usually indigo warp with natural weft. Much softer and lighter than jeans-weight denim. Characteristic indigo fading with wear. Most casual shirt fabric.

parameters.name: trouser_fabric
parameters.description: Fabric types specifically used for trousers, including their formality and seasonal use

values.definition: Standard for dress trousers. Holds crease well. Smooth, resilient. Year-round in appropriate weights.
Gray flannel trousers are the 'blue blazer of cool-weather slacks' per Flusser. Soft, warm, slightly casual. Charcoal most versatile; mid-gray more advanced.
Double-twill weave with parallel diagonal lines. Less shiny than gabardine. Excellent drape and body. More casual versatility than gabardine. Primarily for trousers and overcoats.
Tight twill. Excellent wrinkle resistance. Smooth with visible ridges. Moderate shine. Formal trouser fabric. Cotton gabardine variant for warmer months.
Twill weave cotton. Originally military-grade. The standard business casual trouser. Less formal than wool, more formal than denim.

Pile weave with vertical ridges. Soft, warm. The gentleman's version of jeans per Roetzel. Wide wale more casual; narrow wale slightly dressier. Earth tones classic. Often paired with rough tweed jackets.
Dense cotton satin weave, surface shorn for suede-like finish. Weight: 400+ g/m2. Exceptionally wind-resistant and durable. Not as relaxed as jeans but not dressy. Country and business casual wear.
Flax fiber. Cool, breathable. Wrinkles heavily. Best for summer business casual. Irish linen heavier, wrinkles less. European linen lighter, softer.
Cotton twill, usually indigo. Heaviest jeans-weight to lighter stretch varieties. Most casual trouser fabric. Dark wash dressier than faded.

parameters.name: tie_fabric
parameters.description: Fabric types used for neckties, affecting texture, knot behavior, and formality

values.definition: The standard tie fabric. Smooth with subtle diagonal structure. Holds knot well. Takes dye richly. Moderate to high sheen. Most versatile and formal tie fabric.

Leno weave with open honeycomb structure. Woven exclusively in Lake Como, Italy. Garza fina (smoother) and garza grossa (more visible texture). Uniquely versatile — equally at home with business suits and tweed sport coats. Year-round; unlined for summer.
From wild Tussah silk. Matte finish with small slubs. Less formal than smooth silk twill. More textural. Popular for pocket squares as well. Good with less formal jacketings.
Knitted construction rather than woven. Square or pointed end. Casual texture. Pairs best with tweeds, flannels, and casual sport coats. Not appropriate with smooth business worsted.
Soft, slightly brushed wool in plain weave. Matte surface. Often in paisley or neat patterns. Fall/winter tie. Pairs well with flannel and tweed.
Various constructions. Casual. Summer-appropriate. Matte finish. Pairs with linen suits, cotton sport coats, casual ensembles.
Dry hand, natural slubs. Summer specialist. Casual. Wrinkles in the knot. Pairs with linen and cotton jackets.

parameters.name: fabric_texture_scale
parameters.description: Where a fabric falls on the smooth-to-rough spectrum, which directly maps to formality and combining rules

values.definition: Superfine worsted, broadcloth, silk charmeuse, gabardine. Highest formality. Minimal visible surface texture. Clean, sleek appearance.
Standard worsted, cotton twill, serge, birdseye. Business-formal range. Subtle texture visible only up close.
Flannel, hopsack, cavalry twill, pinpoint oxford, grenadine. The bridge zone between formal and casual. Visible but not dominant texture.
Fresco, Donegal tweed, corduroy (narrow wale), oxford cloth, linen, shantung. Clearly casual texture. Visible pattern in the weave or surface.
Harris tweed, heavy corduroy (wide wale), denim, heavy linen. Most casual. Country and sporting contexts. Robust, utilitarian feel.

parameters.notes: Smoother = more formal. Rougher = more casual. This is one of the most reliable formality indicators. When combining garments, textures should relate — smooth jacket demands smooth tie; textured jacket accepts (even prefers) textured tie.

parameters.name: fabric_sheen_level
parameters.description: The degree of light reflection on the fabric surface, which affects formality and occasion suitability

values.definition: Mohair, silk charmeuse, high-super worsted. Evening wear territory. Dinner jackets, formal accessories. Glamorous under artificial light.
Standard worsted, gabardine, cotton twill. Business-appropriate luster. Professional without being flashy.
Good quality worsted, serge, silk shantung, linen. Natural glow that indicates quality without overt shine.
Flannel, tweed, oxford cloth, fresco, chambray, cotton knit. No shine. Casual, understated. Country and informal contexts.

parameters.notes: More sheen = more formal. Mohair and superfine wools have the most sheen. Matte fabrics read as casual. Evening wear demands some degree of sheen.

parameters.name: fabric_weight_class
parameters.description: The weight category of the fabric, affecting seasonality, drape, and comfort

values.definition: Under 220g/m (under ~7.5oz). Tropical wool, light linen, seersucker, lightweight cotton. Summer use. May lack body for heavy structured tailoring. Requires skill to tailor well.
220-300g/m (~7.5-10oz). Standard worsted, serge, hopsack, cavalry twill. The 3-season sweet spot. ~260g/9oz is the benchmark versatile suiting weight. Drapes well, holds shape.
Over 300g/m (over 10oz). Heavy flannel, tweeds (12-16oz), moleskin (400+g), heavy fresco 3-ply (14-15oz). Fall/winter. Excellent insulation. Stiffer drape. Country and cold-weather wear.

parameters.notes: Weight alone does not determine coolness or warmth — weave openness matters more. A heavy open-weave fresco feels cooler than a lightweight tight-weave super 150s.

parameters.name: fabric_drape_behavior
parameters.description: How the fabric falls and moves on the body, affecting silhouette and visual impression

values.definition: Fresco, mohair, gabardine, Irish linen, dupioni silk. Holds shape away from the body. Creates clean lines and sharp silhouette. Better for structured tailoring.
Cashmere, soft flannel, silk charmeuse, lightweight worsted. Drapes close to the body contours. Creates a softer, more relaxed silhouette. Italian tailoring tradition favors this.
Heavy tweed, denim, waxed cotton, moleskin. Holds its own shape regardless of the body. Creates boxy or structured forms. Country and workwear heritage.

parameters.name: fabric_breathability
parameters.description: How well the fabric allows air circulation, determining comfort in warm conditions

values.definition: Fresco/tropical wool (open plain weave), linen, seersucker, hopsack. Open weave is paramount — gaps between yarns allow air circulation. These are true hot-weather performers.
Mid-weight worsted, cotton broadcloth, oxford cloth, mohair. Adequate for moderate temperatures. Comfortable in climate-controlled environments.
Gabardine (very tight weave), flannel, corduroy, moleskin, heavy tweed. Dense construction traps warmth. Suited to cool and cold conditions.

parameters.notes: Open weave > low weight for breathability. A heavy open-weave fresco is cooler than a lightweight tightly-woven Super 150s.

parameters.name: wrinkle_behavior
parameters.description: How the fabric responds to compression and wear, affecting maintenance demands and appropriate contexts

values.definition: High-twist wools (fresco, tropical), mohair, gabardine, denim. Yarns snap back into shape. Ideal for travel and long-wear days. Fresco and tropical wools excel here.
Standard worsted, flannel, cotton twill, pinpoint oxford, oxford cloth. Normal wrinkling with wear. Can be managed with proper pressing. Acceptable in business contexts.
Linen, broadcloth/poplin, cashmere, lightweight cotton. Wrinkles easily and visibly. Linen wrinkling is considered characterful; broadcloth wrinkling is not. Context determines acceptability.

parameters.name: seasonal_fabric_assignment
parameters.description: Which fabrics are appropriate for each season, based on weight, weave, and thermal properties

values.definition: Tropical/fresco wool, linen, seersucker, cotton (poplin, chambray), hopsack, mohair blends, silk-wool-linen blends. Key: open weave for airflow, lighter colors to reflect heat. Weight secondary to weave openness.
Mid-weight worsted, lighter flannel, cavalry twill, hopsack, cotton gabardine, lighter tweeds, cotton-linen blends. Transitional weight range. Can layer.
Heavy flannel, Harris/Donegal/Cheviot tweed, cashmere, heavy worsted, moleskin, corduroy, velvet. Dense construction for insulation. Heavier weights. Layering with knitwear.
Mid-weight worsted wool (~260g/9oz) is the benchmark. Serge adaptable across weights. Cotton shirting (broadcloth, twill) perennial. Grenadine ties. These form the core of a versatile wardrobe.

parameters.name: fabric_formality_hierarchy
parameters.description: The ranking of suiting/jacketing fabrics from most formal to most casual, which guides occasion-appropriate selection

values.definition: Superfine worsted wool, mohair, mohair blends. Smooth, lustrous, sharp. Evening wear and high business. Clean, sleek surface with natural sheen.
Standard worsted (birdseye, nailhead, pick-and-pick), serge, gabardine. Smooth, professional. The business suit staples. Subtle texture that reads as solid from a distance.
Flannel, cavalry twill, hopsack, high-twist wools. Visible texture begins to casualize. Can still function in business settings. The sport jacket zone.
Linen, smooth cotton, seersucker, lightweight tweeds. Wrinkles, slubs, or puckering make formality impossible. Smart casual and summer occasions.
Heavy tweed (Harris, Donegal), corduroy, denim, moleskin. Country, sporting, and weekend wear. Rough textures, matte surfaces, robust construction.

parameters.notes: Formality hierarchy follows three key axes: smoothness (smoother = more formal), sheen (more shine = more formal), and color (darker = more formal). Pattern adds a fourth: solid > subtle pattern > bold pattern.

parameters.name: shirt_fabric_formality_hierarchy
parameters.description: The ranking of shirt fabrics from most formal to most casual

values.definition: Superfine cotton (high thread count), silk. Smoothest and finest. Formal occasions and executive business.
Broadcloth/poplin, cotton twill. Smooth plain or diagonal weave. Standard business dress shirt fabrics.
Pinpoint oxford, cotton-linen blends. Refined but with casual heritage. Great everyday work shirts.
Oxford cloth, linen, brushed cotton. Visible texture. Sporty or relaxed. Button-down territory.
Chambray, denim, heavy flannel cotton. Most textured and casual. Weekend wear.

parameters.name: fabric_blend_behavior
parameters.description: How blending different fibers modifies fabric properties — used to optimize performance

values.definition: 5-10% cashmere in worsted wool. Adds softness and luxury hand feel without sacrificing the wool's resilience and durability. Best-of-both-worlds blend for jacketing.
Standard Italian mill offering for summer. Lighter weight than pure wool. Linen adds breathability, silk adds luster and drape, wool adds resilience. Less wrinkling than pure linen.
Adds crease resistance and distinctive two-tone luster to wool. 5-15% mohair in commercial blends; 40-70% in premium. Summer suiting and evening wear.
Softens linen's hand feel and reduces wrinkling while retaining coolness. Good for summer shirts and casual trousers. Coolness of linen without the heavy wrinkling.

parameters.name: texture_combination_principle
parameters.description: Rules for combining different fabric textures across garments in an outfit

values.definition: Some texture contrast adds visual interest — a silk grenadine tie with both smooth worsted and rough tweed works because grenadine bridges the texture spectrum. But silk charmeuse with Harris tweed clashes.

Flusser's pattern mixing scale rules extend to texture: the scale of texture should relate to the garment's visual weight. Large-framed men can carry coarser textures; smaller-framed men look better in finer textures.

parameters.name: casual_shirt_fabric
parameters.description: The primary fabric used in casual shirt construction, which affects breathability, texture, weight, seasonality, and overall aesthetic.

values.definition: A basket-weave cotton fabric with a slightly textured surface. Heavier than poplin but softer than denim. Durable, breathable, and gets softer with washing. The classic OCBD fabric. Works across seasons.

A natural fiber woven from flax, known for exceptional breathability and moisture-wicking. Has a distinctive slubby texture and naturally wrinkles. 30% stronger than cotton when dry. Ideal for hot, humid climates like Indian summers. Eco-friendly and biodegradable.

A lightweight plain-weave fabric using single colored and white yarns. Visually resembles denim but is lighter, softer, and more breathable. The weave creates a subtle sheen. Works in warm and transitional weather.

A sturdy twill-weave cotton fabric using indigo-dyed warp and white weft yarns. Heavier and more structured than chambray. Ages beautifully with unique fade patterns. Available in various weights and washes.
A brushed cotton or wool fabric with a soft, napped surface. Provides warmth and insulation. Available in plaid patterns or solid colors. A cold-weather essential with a cozy, rugged character.
A tightly-woven plain-weave fabric with a smooth, crisp finish. Lighter weight than oxford cloth. Provides a cleaner, more polished look for casual shirts. Good for warm weather.

A fabric blending linen and cotton fibers, combining linen's breathability with cotton's softness and structure. More wrinkle-resistant than pure linen. Popular in Indian and tropical markets for balanced performance.
A cotton fabric with a diagonal weave pattern. Heavier and more textured than poplin, with good drape. Suitable for cooler weather casual shirts and overshirts.
A ridged fabric with vertical wales (ribs) cut from extra sets of yarn. Provides warmth, texture, and visual interest. Measured by wale count (wider wales are more casual). A fall/winter fabric.

A puckered cotton fabric with alternating smooth and textured stripes. The puckering allows airflow, making it ideal for hot weather. A classic warm-weather fabric with a distinctly preppy, Southern American heritage.
A semi-synthetic fabric derived from wood pulp. Soft, drapey, and breathable. Commonly used for camp collar and Hawaiian shirts due to its smooth hand-feel and ability to hold vibrant prints.
A sustainable semi-synthetic fiber made from eucalyptus wood pulp. Extremely soft, breathable, and moisture-wicking. Used in premium casual shirts and kurta shirts. Eco-friendly production process.

parameters.name: jeans_stretch
parameters.description: The elasticity level of the denim fabric, determined by the percentage of stretch fibers (typically elastane/spandex) blended with cotton. Affects comfort, mobility, shape retention, and aging character.

values.definition: 100% cotton denim with zero stretch fibers. Heavier weight (12-16 oz). Stiff initially but molds to the body over time. Develops the best natural fading and wear patterns prized by denim enthusiasts. Maximum durability and structure. Requires a break-in period.

Denim blended with 1-2% elastane (typically 98% cotton / 2% elastane). The most common stretch level in men's jeans. Provides slight flexibility and ease of movement while feeling almost as structured as rigid denim. Best balance of shape retention and comfort. Minimal impact on fading potential.

Denim with 3-5% elastane content offering enhanced flexibility and a softer feel. Greater range of motion than comfort stretch. May include dual-core yarn technology for better shape recovery. More prone to shape loss (bagging at knees) over time than lower-stretch options. Less traditional denim feel.

High-performance denim with 5%+ elastane or engineered bi-stretch (4-way stretch) construction. Maximum mobility in all directions. Used in athletic and performance jeans lines. Feels significantly softer and more flexible than traditional denim. Highest risk of shape loss over time.

parameters.name: casual_trouser_fabric
parameters.description: The primary material used in casual trouser construction, affecting comfort, drape, formality, and seasonal appropriateness

values.definition: The classic chino fabric: breathable, durable, soft, and slightly structured. Diagonal weave pattern provides durability while remaining comfortable. The standard for most chinos and khakis.
Cotton twill blended with elastane/lycra for added flexibility and comfort. Retains the look of traditional cotton twill with improved range of motion and shape retention.
Ultra-breathable, naturally cooling fabric with a relaxed drape and characteristic texture. Wrinkles easily but valued for summer comfort. Ideal for warm weather, resort travel, and casual settings.
Linen combined with cotton or synthetic fibers to reduce wrinkling while maintaining breathability. Offers a more practical alternative to pure linen with better shape retention.
Soft, insulating synthetic fabric used primarily in joggers and sweatpants. Brushed interior for warmth and comfort. Best for loungewear and cold-weather casual wear.
Soft, stretchy knit cotton fabric used in joggers and athletic-style pants. Lightweight, comfortable, and flexible. Suited for lounging and casual outings.
Synthetic or blended performance fabrics with moisture-wicking, quick-dry, or four-way stretch properties. Used in modern joggers and athleisure trousers. Suited for active lifestyles and travel.
Cotton fabric with distinctive raised parallel ridges (wales). Available in fine-wale and wide-wale varieties. Provides warmth and texture, ideal for autumn/winter.
Puckered cotton fabric with alternating smooth and textured stripes. The puckered texture allows airflow, making it ideal for hot, humid climates. A seasonal summer fabric.
GOTS-certified organic heavy cotton twill used in sustainable chinos. Maintains the same properties as conventional cotton twill but grown without synthetic pesticides or fertilizers.

parameters.name: leather_jacket_material
parameters.description: The specific type of leather or skin used in jacket construction, affecting durability, texture, weight, and price

values.definition: The highest grade of leather, using the complete outer surface of the hide with natural grain intact. Most durable, develops a rich patina over time, and molds to the wearer's body. The gold standard for leather jackets.
Softer, lighter, and more supple than cowhide. Offers a more refined, luxurious feel. Less durable than cowhide but provides superior drape and comfort. Often used in fashion-forward styles.
Sheep or lamb skin shorn once then tanned with wool intact. Leather on one side, soft insulating wool on the other. Dense, even wool provides superior warmth. Used in aviator and lined jacket styles.

Leather with a napped, velvety finish created from the inner surface of the hide. Softer texture and a more casual appearance than smooth leather. Requires more care and is less water-resistant. Popular for bomber styles.
Durable leather with a distinctive pebbled grain texture. Lighter than cowhide but highly resistant to abrasion. Develops character and patina with wear. A practical choice for daily-wear jackets.

parameters.name: casual_jacket_fabric
parameters.description: The primary material used in non-leather casual jacket construction, affecting weather protection, durability, and style

values.definition: Lightweight synthetic fabric used in bombers, windbreakers, and coach jackets. Water-resistant, quick-drying, and durable. The original MA-1 bomber material. Often has a slight sheen.
Sturdy cotton twill fabric used in trucker and jean jackets. Raw denim develops unique fades and wear marks over time. Available in various weights and washes. A heritage workwear fabric.

Heavy-duty woven cotton used in chore coats, barn jackets, and field jackets. Durable and sturdy with a matte finish. Often used in workwear-inspired pieces. Can be unlined or lined with flannel/quilting.

Cotton fabric treated with beeswax or paraffin coating for water resistance. Develops a unique patina with wear as the wax creases and ages. Needs periodic re-waxing. Used in field jackets, truckers, and country-style jackets.

Natural fiber used in varsity jacket bodies, overcoats, and some chore coats (boiled wool). Provides warmth and structure. Heavier than cotton alternatives. Includes blended wool options for lighter-weight garments.
Synthetic fabric used in fleece jackets and hoodie linings. Soft, insulating, and lightweight. Available in different pile heights. Associated with outdoor and gorpcore styling.
Structured woven cotton used in chore jackets and field jackets. Heavier than standard cotton, offering better wind resistance and durability. Includes drill and duck canvas variants.
Soft, brushed cotton or wool fabric used in shackets and shirt jackets. Provides warmth without excessive weight. Often in plaid patterns. Creates a relaxed, heritage aesthetic.
Ribbed cotton fabric used in some overshirts and shackets. Adds texture and warmth. Available in various wale widths. A vintage-inspired fabric choice for casual jackets.

Natural down insulation used inside puffer jackets and some quilted jackets. Provides exceptional warmth-to-weight ratio. Traps body heat in the baffled chambers. The standard insulation for high-performance cold-weather jackets.

parameters.name: hoodie_fabric_weight
parameters.description: The weight classification of hoodie fabric measured in grams per square meter, determining warmth, structure, and appropriate use

values.definition: Under 300 g/m2. Ideal for spring, layering, or workouts. Thin and breathable, not suitable as standalone cold-weather wear. Best for active use and warm-weather layering.
300-400 g/m2. Balanced warmth and comfort for year-round wear. The most versatile weight class. Suitable as a standalone layer in mild weather or as a mid-layer in cold weather.
400 g/m2 and above. Structured, premium feel. Perfect for outerwear looks where the hoodie serves as the main jacket. Provides substantial warmth and has a boxy, substantial silhouette.

parameters.name: hoodie_fabric_type
parameters.description: The primary fabric material used in hoodie construction, affecting softness, warmth, durability, and performance characteristics

values.definition: Classic hoodie fabric that is soft, breathable, and comfortable. Natural fiber that absorbs moisture. Best for everyday casual wear. Available in various weights.
Fabric with a soft brushed interior providing excellent insulation and comfort. Can pill if low-quality. Best for cold weather and lounging. The most popular hoodie fabric for warmth.
Looped-back knit fabric that is lighter and more breathable than fleece. Smooth on the outside with looped pile on the inside. Ideal for transitional weather and active wear.

Cotton blended with polyester for improved durability, shape retention, and reduced shrinkage. Offers a balance of cotton's comfort with polyester's performance properties. The most common hoodie fabric blend.
Synthetic or blended fabrics engineered to draw moisture away from the body. Quick-drying and breathable. Designed for workouts and athletic use. Often features stretch properties.

parameters.name: indian_climate_fabric_preference
parameters.description: Fabric types best suited for each Indian season, mapped by their climate-responsive properties including breathability, moisture management, drying speed, and thermal regulation

values.definition: Most preferred fabric for Indian summers; super absorbent, breathable, gentle on skin; pulls sweat away from body; handloom cotton has superior breathability due to unique texture enhancing airflow. Suitable for peak summer and monsoon (tightly woven varieties). GSM range 120-200 for summer shirts

MVP of Indian summer dressing; extremely lightweight and breathable with hollow-core fibers exceptional at wicking and drying. Natural flax fiber that circulates air keeping body cool. Charming crumple adds casual elegance. Best for peak summer; debated for monsoon as some sources warn it shrinks in water while others praise its moisture-wicking

India's iconic handspun and handwoven fabric; lightweight with maximum airflow through characteristic gaps between fibers from handloom process. Adapts to weather - stays cool in summer, warm in winter making it year-round essential. Mesh-like texture lets air pass through, comfortable during monsoons. Excellent moisture absorption and quick-drying despite being handmade

Gaining popularity for Indian climate; softer than cotton, breathable with built-in odor resistance and natural UV protection. Temperature regulating - cool in summer, warm in winter. Naturally hypoallergenic and excellent moisture-wicking. Best for activewear and casual summer clothing. Biodegradable and wrinkle-resistant

Superior blend for Indian office heat combining linen's exceptional wicking with cotton's softness; reduces linen's tendency to wrinkle badly while maintaining breathability. Adds a touch of polish appropriate for office environments. Ideal for AC-to-outdoor transition scenarios

Performance polyester and nylon blends designed to wick moisture away and dry quickly; particularly beneficial during monsoon season when natural fibers may stay damp. Cotton-polyester blends offer a practical middle ground. Best for athleisure monsoon wear and active commuting

Fabrics specifically engineered for rapid drying during monsoon season; includes polyester-cotton blends, nylon blends, and performance knits. Essential for monsoon commuting and travel. Should be lightweight, breathable, and wrinkle-resistant

Modern eco-friendly fabric from wood pulp (eucalyptus); wicks moisture 40% faster than regular cotton with naturally cool hand feel. Non-transparent despite being lightweight, exceptionally soft and cooling. Micro-vent channel technology emerging for 2025. Excellent for Indian summer office and casual wear

Strong, sustainable, and as breathable as linen; growing global fashion trend in 2025. Suitable for Indian summer casual and office wear. Natural fiber with excellent durability and environmental credentials
Puckered texture keeps fabric off skin, creating natural air circulation channels. Excellent for summer blazers and office wear in Indian climate. Adds visual depth and texture without weight
Open-weave fabric ideal for summer blazers; lightweight and breathable enough for Indian heat. Adds texture and visual interest suitable for business casual office environments

Cotton-made fabric with slightly denser weave than standard cotton; medium-weight with excellent drape and smoother feel. Super soft with above-average airiness and breathability. Good for casual and office wear in Indian summers

parameters.name: casual_fabric_type
parameters.description: Specific fabric types used in casual menswear, categorized by construction method, fiber content, and suitability for Indian climate conditions

values.definition: Single-knit fabric from one continuous set of yarns forming interlocking loops; smooth on outside, slightly open texture inside for breathability without compromising structure. Lightweight and flexible, making it ideal for everyday casual T-shirts in Indian heat. Soft hand feel with good drape

Raised weave fabric with waffle, honeycomb, or corded texture that provides depth and visual richness. Open knit structure allows superior airflow, making it one of the most breathable premium cotton fabrics for Indian hot and humid conditions. Typical weight 220-260 GSM. Standard fabric for quality polo shirts

Cotton knit with characteristic loops on inside and smooth jersey-like outside. Super soft, breathable, flexible, absorbent, and durable. Slightly heavier than jersey with internal loops that capture moisture and trap air. Can handle serious GSM (up to 480gsm for premium). Best for joggers, sweatshirts, and loungewear. The terry cloth texture is practical for monsoon as it dries quickly

Soft, insulating knit fabric best suited for Indian winter (north) and post-monsoon chill. Not appropriate for summer or monsoon due to heat retention. Used in hoodies, jackets, and layering pieces for cold weather. Synthetic fleece dries faster than natural alternatives

Engineered poly-cotton or poly-nylon blends with moisture-wicking technology; designed for active wear and monsoon conditions. Combines natural fiber comfort with synthetic quick-dry properties. Used in athleisure polo shirts, joggers, and activewear. Ideal for humid Indian conditions where pure cotton stays damp

Softer than cotton with natural antimicrobial, UV-protective, and temperature-regulating properties. Excellent moisture-wicking that keeps skin dry in Indian humidity. Hypoallergenic and wrinkle-resistant. Used in casual T-shirts, base layers, joggers, and undergarments. Biodegradable and sustainable

Semi-synthetic fabric from beech tree pulp with exceptional softness and tighter weave than bamboo. More absorbent than cotton, making it good for hot and humid Indian days. Greater consistency, durability, and performance over time compared to bamboo. Popular for undergarments, base layers, and body-contact casual wear

Eco-friendly cellulose fabric from wood pulp (commonly eucalyptus, branded as Tencel). Wicks moisture 40% faster than regular cotton. Lightweight but non-transparent, exceptionally soft with silk-like feel and natural cooling effect. Produced via closed-loop sustainable process. Excellent for summer T-shirts and casual shirts in Indian heat. Works well blended with cotton

India's heritage handspun and handwoven fabric; characteristic irregular texture from manual techniques. Gaps between hand-woven fibers create natural airflow channels. Adapts to climate - cool in summer, warm in winter. Usually slightly thicker than machine-made fabrics but still highly breathable. Cultural significance adds style dimension beyond mere function

Lightweight plain-weave cotton fabric resembling denim but much lighter and more breathable. Suitable for casual monsoon shirts as it handles moisture better than heavy denim. Provides structured casual look without weight penalty in Indian heat

Towel-like looped fabric used in casual shorts and loungewear; on-trend for monsoon season as it absorbs moisture and dries quickly. Relaxed aesthetic suited for casual outings during rain. Heavier than jersey but with superior moisture handling

parameters.name: casual_fabric_weight
parameters.description: Weight classification of casual fabrics measured in GSM (grams per square meter), affecting comfort, drape, breathability, and seasonal appropriateness in Indian climate

values.definition: Under 150 GSM; fabrics like voile, lightweight linen, and sheer cotton. Maximum breathability for peak Indian summer (40C+). May sacrifice opacity and structure. Best for layered looks where transparency is managed. Ideal for base layers and undershirts in extreme heat

150-200 GSM; standard range for summer T-shirts, casual shirts, and polos in Indian climate. Includes jersey cotton tees, lightweight bamboo, lyocell, and modal garments. Balances breathability with adequate coverage and structure. The sweet spot for everyday Indian summer casual wear

200-300 GSM; includes pique cotton polos (220-260 GSM), standard french terry, cotton poplin, and structured casual shirts. Provides more body and texture while remaining manageable in Indian heat. Suitable for smart casual office wear and AC environments. Works for monsoon season where slightly heavier fabrics resist rain better

Over 300 GSM; includes premium french terry (400-480 GSM), fleece, heavyweight cotton, and dense knits. Too warm for Indian summer outdoor wear but appropriate for north Indian winter, post-monsoon evenings, and heavily air-conditioned environments. Used in joggers, hoodies, and sweatshirts for layering

parameters.name: casual_fabric_breathability
parameters.description: Breathability rating of casual fabrics specifically mapped to Indian climate needs, where high humidity demands both air permeability and moisture management to prevent discomfort

values.definition: Maximum air circulation and moisture management; essential for Indian peak summer and monsoon humidity. Includes: linen (hollow-core fibers exceptional at wicking), khadi (hand-woven gaps create natural airflow), bamboo (temperature-regulating with natural wicking), lyocell/Tencel (wicks 40% faster than cotton), lightweight cotton, and seersucker (puckered texture lifts fabric off skin). These fabrics actively cool the body through evaporative mechanisms

Good air circulation suitable for Indian transitional seasons, AC environments, and moderate humidity. Includes: pique cotton (open knit aids airflow but denser than plain weave), french terry (loops add insulation reducing breathability vs jersey), modal (tight weave is absorbent but less airy), cotton-polyester blends (synthetic component slightly reduces airflow), poplin (denser weave than standard cotton). Adequate for office wear where AC moderates temperature

Limited air circulation; inappropriate for Indian summer outdoor wear. Includes: polyester (traps heat, retains moisture), heavy fleece, dense synthetics, heavy denim, and unlined synthetic jackets. These fabrics cause discomfort in Indian heat and humidity by trapping body heat and moisture against skin. Only appropriate for north Indian deep winter or specific rain-protection layers worn briefly

fabric_behavior_principles.name: smoothness_formality_correlation
fabric_behavior_principles.description: The single most reliable predictor of formality is surface smoothness. Smoother fabrics are always more formal than rougher ones of the same fiber. This holds across all garment types — suits, shirts, trousers, ties. A smooth worsted is more formal than a textured flannel; broadcloth is more formal than oxford cloth.

fabric_behavior_principles.name: weave_trumps_weight
fabric_behavior_principles.description: For breathability and summer comfort, the openness of the weave matters more than the weight of the fabric. A heavy (9-10oz) open-weave fresco feels cooler than a lightweight (6oz) tightly woven super 150s. This is counterintuitive but critical for summer fabric selection.

fabric_behavior_principles.name: texture_coherence_in_ensembles
fabric_behavior_principles.description: CANONICAL PRINCIPLE (referenced by D04, D09). All elements of an outfit should inhabit a compatible texture zone. Smooth jacket demands smooth tie and smooth-to-moderate shirt. Textured tweed jacket accepts (and benefits from) wool knit tie, flannel trousers, and oxford shirt. Mixing across extreme texture zones (silk charmeuse tie with Harris tweed) creates dissonance. Keep all elements within the same texture band for coherence.

texture_band_examples.smooth_band: Worsted suit + broadcloth shirt + silk twill tie + polished calfskin shoes
texture_band_examples.moderate_band: Flannel suit + pinpoint oxford shirt + grenadine tie + suede shoes
texture_band_examples.textured_band: Tweed jacket + oxford cloth shirt + wool knit tie + brogues

fabric_behavior_principles.name: pattern_is_texture
fabric_behavior_principles.description: Flusser's Ch4 insight: pattern mixing and texture mixing follow the same principles. Both are visual stimuli that must be harmonized through scale and contrast. A boldly patterned fabric adds visual 'weight' similar to a coarse texture. The more patterns/textures in an ensemble, the more skill required.

fabric_behavior_principles.name: natural_fiber_supremacy
fabric_behavior_principles.description: In classic menswear, natural fibers (wool, cotton, linen, silk) are universally preferred over synthetics. Natural fibers breathe better, drape more naturally, age more gracefully, and take dye more richly. Quality is expressed through fiber choice — cashmere, mohair, Sea Island cotton, Irish linen signal refinement.

fabric_behavior_principles.name: fabric_as_formality_lever
fabric_behavior_principles.description: Fabric choice is one of the most powerful tools for shifting formality without changing garment type. The same blazer silhouette in mohair reads as evening wear, in worsted as business, in hopsack as smart casual, and in corduroy as country casual. Fabric transforms context more efficiently than cut.

Plain weave → smooth; pile → textured; herringbone → moderate
Open weave → excellent; tight twill → low
Twill resists wrinkles; plain weave more prone
Heavy fabrics tend stiffer; light tend flowing
Blend rules depend on base fiber

Each shirting fabric maps to a shirt formality tier
Trouser fabrics follow same formality hierarchy
